about: Sources for the energy-options study (energy_options.md, energy_options.py), searched on 5 November 2026 within the study's literature allowance. 'access' says how far each was read: most were read only as search-result summaries or abstracts, and their values are used as published figures at that depth. Values the study recalls without a source checked this session are labelled 'recalled' in the product's assumptions.

sources.use: Commercial wafer-based modules from new production reached 22% in 2024; energy payback about 1 year in Europe (0.9-1.1 years by location)
sources.access: search-result summary of the report (not opened)

sources.citation: Mirletz, Ovaitt, Sridhar & Barnes 2022, Circular economy priorities for photovoltaics in the energy transition, PLoS ONE 17, e0274351
sources.use: 1.75 TW of US PV by 2050 demands 97 Mt of virgin material cumulatively, about 55 t per MW of modules

sources.citation: Search summaries of PV material intensity (Smart Energy Council 2026, aluminium in solar panels; LCA summaries)
sources.use: About 21 t of aluminium per MW (18-35 by mounting); 60-67 t of steel, 4-5 t of copper and 6-8 t of aluminium per MW of panels
sources.access: search-result summaries (not opened); used only for the order of magnitude

sources.citation: Fraunhofer ISE 2021, Record efficiency of 68.9% for GaAs thin-film photovoltaic cell under laser light (48th IEEE PVSC; Helmers et al. 2021)
sources.use: The best laser power converter: 68.9% under 858 nm laser light
sources.access: search-result summaries of the press release

sources.citation: DARPA POWER programme 2025, optical power beaming record (The Register, 19 May 2025; NRL news)
sources.use: More than 800 W delivered over 8.6 km for 30 s; just over 20% from laser output to electricity at the receiver, at shorter distances

sources.citation: Laser wall-plug efficiencies: a 780 nm GaAsP laser diode at 71% (Optics and Laser Technology 2023); IPG YLS-ECO fibre lasers above 50%
sources.use: Transmitter efficiencies for an optical link, 50-70%
sources.access: search-result summaries and the article's listing

sources.citation: Brown 1977 rectenna record, as cited in rectenna reviews (90.6% at 2.45 GHz with 8 W input, GaAs-Pt Schottky diode); an 82% rectenna at 5.8 GHz
sources.use: Rectenna element efficiencies at the two bands; the screen keeps the power screen's 85% at both
sources.access: search-result summaries of reviews; Rodenbeck et al. 2021 (power_sources.json) carries the field's review

sources.citation: Caltech Space Solar Power Project 2023, MAPLE demonstrates wireless power transfer in space
sources.use: The first wireless power transfer in space (milliwatts to LEDs about 30 cm away, detectable power to Earth): maturity of space power beaming
sources.access: search-result summaries of the news release

sources.citation: US Congress OTA 1981, Solar Power Satellites (NTIS PB82-108846)
sources.use: The 1978 reference satellite at about 5e4 t for 5 GW (0.1 kW/kg); its rectenna an ellipse of about 10 by 13 km on continuous concrete footings
sources.access: search-result summaries only; the rectenna's materials were not found and stay a design guess

sources.citation: ITER Organization 2024, Baseline 2024 press conference summary
sources.use: Start of research operation in 2034, deuterium-tritium operation in 2039
sources.access: search-result summaries of the summary and of IPP's note

sources.citation: LLNL 2025, National Ignition Facility annual report FY2025
sources.use: 8.6 MJ from 2.08 MJ of laser energy on 7 April 2025, a target gain of 4.13; no net electricity at the wall

sources.citation: Langseth, Keihm & Peters 1976, Revised lunar heat-flow values, Proc. Lunar Sci. Conf. 7, 3143; Siegler & Smrekar 2014, JGR Planets 119, 47
sources.use: Apollo 15 and 17 heat flow, 21 and 14-16 mW/m2; an internal heat flow of 9-13 mW/m2 after the crust's effects

sources.citation: Lawrence et al., Lunar Prospector gamma-ray thorium maps, as summarised by Chevrel et al. 2002 and later work
sources.use: The Procellarum KREEP Terrane holds 4-12 ppm thorium at the surface, about 5.5 on average

sources.citation: Miller & Keith 2018, Climatic impacts of wind power, Joule 2, 2618; Miller & Keith 2018, Environ. Res. Lett. 13, 104008
sources.use: Large wind farms realise about 0.5 W/m2 (US farms in 2016); modelled onshore 0.32-0.37 W/m2

sources.citation: Rajagopalan & Nihous 2013, Estimates of global OTEC resources using an ocean general circulation model, Renewable Energy 50, 532
sources.use: Global OTEC net power peaks at 12-14 TW; about 7 TW without much effect on ocean temperatures

sources.citation: Form Energy iron-air battery, round-trip efficiency (Energy-Storage.news and other secondary sources, 2023-2026)
sources.use: 100-hour iron-air storage at about 40-45% round trip

sources.use: Earth's mean wind power density, 323 W/m2 over the atlas's whole area and 410 W/m2 over its windiest half, the comparison for the Moon's low winds
